findings.issue: いる is misanalyzed as the animate-existence verb (がいる pattern). With inanimate ピザ it must be 要る 'to need/want': ピザがいる人 = 'person who wants/needs pizza' (cf. en 'who wants pizza?'). Existential いる cannot take ピザ as subject; the 'person for whom there is pizza' reading is false grammar.
findings.current: uses the target pattern がいる to indicate the existence of a person: 'ピザがいる人' = 'the person for whom there is pizza / who wants pizza'
findings.suggested: Here いる is 要る ('to need/want'), not existential いる (animate-only): ピザがいる人 = 'person who needs/wants pizza'.

findings.issue: Same wrong grammar fact as expl_en: analyzes いる as 'existir, para seres vivos' although the subject is inanimate ピザ; the verb is 要る 'precisar/querer'. Teaches a false rule about existential いる.
findings.current: A frase usa o padrão-alvo がいる para indicar a existência de uma pessoa: 'ピザがいる人' = 'a pessoa para quem há pizza / que quer pizza'
findings.suggested: Aqui いる é 要る ('precisar/querer'), não o いる de existência (só para seres vivos): ピザがいる人 = 'pessoa que precisa/quer pizza'.

findings.issue: Gloss gives the animate-existence sense of いる, which is impossible with inanimate ピザ; in context the verb is 要る 'to need/want'.
findings.current: there to be; to exist (for living beings)

findings.issue: Gloss 'haver; existir (para seres vivos)' is the wrong sense in context; いる here is 要る 'precisar/querer'.
Reading field contains the kanji 人 itself instead of its reading; in context 人 = ひと (the kana line correctly has ひと).

Sense inversion: ～ないほうがいい means 'the not-doing side is good' (better NOT to do it), and じゃないかな is only a softening tag. 'It's no good not doing it' attaches the negation to 'good' and advises the opposite of the Japanese.
findings.current: It's no good not doing it this way, right?
findings.suggested: The side of not doing it that way is good, isn't it, I wonder?

findings.issue: The negation of the tag じゃない is wrongly prefixed to the ほうがいい block ('não-lado-de-ser-bom' = 'não é bom'), garbling/inverting the structure; the 'good' predicate is affirmative, only the tag is negative.
findings.current: Assim não fazer não-lado-de-ser-bom, não é mesmo, hein?
findings.suggested: Assim não fazer — (esse) lado é bom, não é?, hein.

findings.issue: Wrong person: the sentence is self-directed regret (～ばよかったなあ; en 'I should have come', expl says speaker regret), but lit_en renders it as 'if you'd come', contradicting every other field.
findings.current: It would have been nice if you'd come by bicycle, huh.
findings.suggested: It would have been nice if (I) had come by bicycle, huh.

findings.issue: 'Don't go up, will you?' reads in English as a prohibition + tag (request NOT to go up), but お上がりになりませんか is a negative-question invitation ('won't you go up/come in?').
'has (wants) pizza' carries over the wrong existential/possession reading; 要る means 'to need', as the lit_pt correctly renders ('precisa de').
findings.current: Well, the person who has (wants) pizza (!)

findings.issue: Reads as an imperative ('Try doing it once more.'), but the Japanese is a declarative first-person intention (en: 'I will try again'); the literal mirror flips the mood and implied subject.
Missing space before the parenthesis in the pt gloss.
'without だ' is misleading after a verb: だ can never follow みる, so the remark implies a nonexistent option. Should say plain (non-polite) form instead.
findings.current: The dictionary form みる at the end, without だ, gives an informal tone of decision/intent ('I'll try').
findings.suggested: The dictionary form みる at the end (plain, non-polite form) gives an informal tone of decision/intent ('I'll try').

findings.issue: Same as expl_en: 'sem だ' sugere que だ poderia seguir o verbo みる, o que é agramatical; deve dizer forma simples/sem polidez.
findings.current: A forma de dicionário みる no fim, sem だ, dá um tom de decisão/intenção informal ('vou tentar').
findings.suggested: A forma de dicionário みる no fim (forma simples, sem ます/polidez) dá um tom de decisão/intenção informal ('vou tentar').

findings.issue: Object particle を left as を instead of the corpus phonetic convention お (は→わ, へ→え, を→お); the romaji already uses 'o' (kuchio...). Inconsistent with the rest of the bank.
findings.current: くちをゆすがなくちゃ。
findings.suggested: くちおゆすがなくちゃ。

findings.issue: それ is the medial demonstrative 'that/it'; 'this' corresponds to これ and is wrong in a gloss for それ (a distinction the course teaches).
